question.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{Var}[X].$ 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{8},\, & 0\le x\le 4, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

First, we compute $\text{E}[X]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{0}^{4}x\cdot \frac{x}{8}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}\frac{{x}^{2}}{8}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{3}}{24}|}_{0}^{4} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{x}{8}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}\frac{{x}^{3}}{8}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{4}}{32}|}_{0}^{4} \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =8-{(\frac{8}{3})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{8}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$
